markdown_report:
**Proposal: evidence-gated directed transition residual for SASRec.** At 0% progress, retain a small extension, but strengthen candidate-specific evidence and bound its contribution. Gains remain unmeasured hypotheses.

**Insights from the starting point.** (1) SASRec already models ordered preferences; an explicit transition branch needs demonstrated complementarity. (2) User feedback identifies broad relevance displacing current intent and unsupported practical associations. Recent, repeatedly observed successors may address both, without establishing compatibility or unmet need. (3) Electronics has 14.95% negative-over-positive rankings versus 3.03% for Movies_and_TV. Similar embedding-similarity scores do not support prioritizing collapse remedies.

**Insights from related work.** (1) [TGCL4SR](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/28789) motivates transition–sequence fusion; [FPMC](https://archives.iw3c2.org/www2010/pub/pdfs/RendleFreudenthaler2010-FPMC.pdf) and [FOSSIL](https://arxiv.org/abs/1609.09152) establish substantial precedent for directed factors and preference fusion. (2) [FamouSRec](https://doi.org/10.1145/3696410.3714663) motivates adaptive routing, but source frequency alone cannot justify individual successors. (3) [gSASRec](https://www.ijcai.org/proceedings/2024/0939.pdf) motivates objective controls; improved training margins cannot establish validation gains.

Three directions follow: current-intent modeling, evidence-dependent fusion, and ranking supervision. The framework separates **personal sequence evidence**, **population successor evidence**, and **candidate discrimination**. Its central gap is determining when population evidence supports a particular recommendation.

Scores are originality/potential/user alignment/model alignment/difficulty; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

| Idea | Scores | Positive assessment | Negative assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| Evidence-gated transition residual | 4/7/7/7/6 | O: explicit candidate evidence; P: extensible fusion; U: recent intent and supported successors; M: confusing candidates; D: compact expert | O: extensive precedent; P: sparse edges; U: compatibility unresolved; M: gains unproven; D: sparse lookup and export |
| Recent/stable preference gate | 4/7/7/6/3 | O: task adaptation; P: reusable; U: current and sustained preferences; M: possible interference reduction; D: simple pooling | O: familiar; P: uncertain benefit; U: weak practical grounding; M: interference unverified; D: causal masking |
| Multi-negative gBCE | 3/7/4/8/2 | O: controlled adaptation; P: useful baseline; U: sharper ranking; M: weak-margin target; D: localized change | O: published; P: incremental; U: indirect alignment; M: false negatives; D: scoring cost |

Select the transition residual because it explicitly targets two user failures—broad associations displacing recent intent and unsupported practical associations—and weak positive–negative separation. Count distinct training users per directed edge. Multiply a normalized, bounded transition score by source-support and candidate-edge shrinkage. Unseen edges receive no residual; SASRec retains generalization. This restriction limits only the residual, and cannot guarantee safe or useful recommendations.

Prespecify sequence-only, fixed-fusion, scalar-gate and learned-gate ablations, with auxiliary loss initially disabled. Treat untied/parameter-matched SASRec, FMC/FOSSIL and auxiliary-loss controls as follow-ups within budget. Preserve routing, seeds, diagnostic interfaces and predictor parity. Match GPU-second allocations and validation opportunities; freeze checkpoint rules and tie-breaking before trials. Select exclusively by pinned macro validation HR@10. Paired user-bootstrap intervals quantify fixed-seed uncertainty, not selection bias ([Cawley–Talbot](https://www.jmlr.org/papers/v11/cawley10a.html)); sampled ranking need not transfer to full-catalog ranking ([Krichene–Rendle](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/)).

idea.description: Add a bounded, evidence-gated directed transition residual to per-dataset SASRec. Separate source and target embeddings encode asymmetric successor relationships. Source support, candidate-specific distinct-user edge support, and a small causal gate control the residual. Preserve SASRec as the generalizing pathway when transition evidence is absent.
idea.motivation: The user diagnosis identifies broad associations outranking recent intent and practical recommendations lacking behavioral support. Conditioning on the most recent item and repeatedly observed directed successors explicitly targets these two failures. The quantitative target is weak positive–negative separation, especially Electronics' 14.95% wrong-ranking rate and negative lower-tail margin. Transition evidence cannot establish compatibility, ownership, product dimensions, replacement needs, or whether a purchase already satisfied a need. The proposal does not claim to solve those remaining failures.
idea.implementation_notes:
Retain the original per-category SASRec backbone, sampled loss, optimizer, negative sampler and training examples initially. Use only public training histories, titles, descriptions and timestamps; metadata examples mentioning ratings, categories, prices, stores or reviews do not authorize those unavailable fields. No semantic branch is required for this first experiment.

For each category, create the set of nonpadding adjacent ordered item pairs observed for each training user. Increment c_ij once per user per pair, preventing repeated interactions by one user from dominating that edge. Define C_i = sum_j c_ij; this is total user-edge support, not the number of distinct users for the source. Store counts in a sorted sparse representation and serialize it beneath the trial directory. Training-only aggregate counts may include all training interactions, as population statistics; sequence features at position t must use only the prefix through t. Never include validation or test interactions in these counts.

At each valid position use the current item i_t as source. Set source reliability to C_i/(C_i+lambda) and edge reliability to c_ij/(c_ij+kappa). Define a normalized transition score as cosine(source_embedding[i], target_embedding[j]), with normalization epsilon 1e-8. Multiply it by a learned positive scale bounded by A_max, both reliability terms, and a sigmoid gate. The gate inputs are the SASRec state, log1p(C_i), and log1p(prefix_length); use a single linear layer with bias. Candidate-specific reliability remains outside that gate. Consequently the residual magnitude is at most A_max and exactly zero for an unobserved edge. This does not restrict unsupported scores arising through SASRec itself. Initialize source/target embeddings with the baseline embedding initializer; initialize gate weights and bias to zero, and initialize the scale to 0.01 through an inverse-sigmoid parameterization. Separate source/target embeddings provide directionality, but are established machinery rather than the principal novelty. Tied SASRec item embeddings do not imply symmetric sequence scores.

For a concrete initial configuration, fix lambda=10, kappa=3 and A_max=2.0 before trials; these are proposed engineering defaults, not evidence-based optima. Do not sweep them in the first ablation. Disable the auxiliary transition loss initially to isolate architectural effects. If subsequently enabled, use the same observed positives and training negatives, the same valid-position mask, and source-support-weighted baseline BCE on transition scores, with weight 0.1 and normalization by the number of valid positions. Report auxiliary-on/off comparisons separately; otherwise supervision and architecture are confounded. Retain baseline negative sampling for matched controls. Any later sampler change must exclude padding, target collisions and observed training positives without consulting held-out interactions; unseen negatives remain uncertain.

Source frequency can create popularity shortcuts even with edge shrinkage. Track source/target frequency strata, residual magnitude, gate saturation and edge coverage alongside the original margins. Distinct-user support and bounded scores mitigate particular shortcuts but do not eliminate popularity bias. An optional later count-only control can use clipped, smoothed log-lift: p0(j)=(sum_i c_ij+1)/(sum_ij c_ij+N), p_tilde(j|i)=(c_ij+alpha*p0(j))/(C_i+alpha), and clip(log(p_tilde/p0),-b,b). Keep it a separate ablation rather than adding another component to the initial model. Entropy measures concentration, not calibrated confidence; defer entropy gating.

Preserve DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, all four dataset routes, and int(os.environ.get('SASREC_EPOCHS', '200')). Keep execution single-GPU and save parameters, support tables, item mappings and configuration beneath the trial directory. The predictor writer must instantiate and reload this exact architecture, including counts, normalization, gate and scale.

Keep DiagnosisProbe(view, device).run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), returning metrics and metric_definitions. view.model must be the trained module. Preserve view.item_emb and the B x L diagnostic loader contract. Implement log2feats as a packed tensor containing SASRec state, normalized source vector, gate, source reliability and source item ID; predict_score must unpack it and retrieve candidate edge support. An integer ID packed into a floating tensor requires an exactly representable dtype and a runtime round-trip check; alternatively use a documented structured feature object and adapt every caller and probe consistently. Prefer the structured representation if existing adapters permit it. Probe margins must use the complete predict_score path. Identify the baseline item table in embedding-similarity definitions. Category breakdowns are unavailable and must be omitted or explicitly marked unavailable; do not synthesize categories or simulator traits. Keep existing metric names and definitions where their computation remains unchanged, and document any added measures.

Prespecify four initial variants: unchanged SASRec, residual with gate fixed at 1, residual with a learned global sigmoid scalar, and residual with the feature-conditioned gate. All residual variants retain source/edge shrinkage, normalized vectors and the same bounded scale. Use identical baseline hyperparameters and no auxiliary loss. Give each variant at most 9,000 GPU-seconds across its four categories, split equally by category, reserving 7,200 GPU-seconds of the shared 43,200 for diagnostics, debugging and failures. Charge every GPU cost to that budget; do not recycle savings into adaptive searches. Stop each category at 200 epochs or its 2,250 GPU-second cap, whichever comes first. Validate the latest complete four-category checkpoint at cumulative training caps of 750, 1,500 and 2,250 GPU-seconds per category; if training finishes earlier, reuse the finished checkpoint rather than creating additional selection opportunities. Select among recorded checkpoints by macro validation HR@10; exact ties prefer unchanged SASRec, then fewer learned gate parameters, then the earlier checkpoint. Reserve follow-up controls for a separately prespecified reallocation before trials, rather than implying the entire control matrix fits this initial allocation. If the actual baseline runtime makes these caps impractical, revise the schedule once before execution and log that revision.

Log configurations, software versions, complete checkpoints and all costs; report score versus cumulative compute. If the pinned evaluator exposes per-user hit indicators, retain paired hits for identical candidates. Bootstrap 200 users independently within each category, using identical resampled indices across models, then average the four category differences equally. Use 10,000 replicates, a separate analysis RNG seed 42 and percentile 95% intervals; report category deltas and discordant hit counts. One hit changes category HR by 0.005 and macro HR by 0.00125. These intervals condition on fixed training and candidate seeds and do not correct adaptive winner selection. Do not modify the evaluator to obtain unavailable outputs or fabricate intervals.

Verify exported predictor raw scores against the training evaluation path, and compare candidate scores against full-catalog scores restricted to identical IDs. Use float32 evaluation with atol=1e-5 and rtol=1e-4, recording maximum errors and ranking disagreements. Cover residual enabled/disabled, all category routes, item indexing, padding/truncation, last valid position, seen-item masks, ties, reloads, batching and catalog chunking. Any top-10 disagreement requires resolution before accepting the export. Keep pinned validation candidates and seed 42 unchanged. Sampled validation and twenty-user full-catalog simulator feedback are different observations; select only by the common macro validation HR@10. Freeze the winner before the host's separate final held-out evaluation. No benchmark gain has been measured.
idea.pseudocode:
# Reproducible algorithm specification; host trainer and predictor writer share this scorer.
# Fixed first-trial settings: lambda=10, kappa=3, A_max=2.0, auxiliary_weight=0.
# Preserve baseline loss, optimizer, sampler, architecture settings, and seed handling.

for category in FOUR_CATEGORIES:
    edge_count = Counter()
    for user, history in training_histories[category].items():
        pairs = {(i, j) for i, j in adjacent(history) if i != 0 and j != 0}
        for pair in pairs:
            edge_count[pair] += 1
    source_support = sum_edge_counts_by_source(edge_count)
    model = SASRecWithDirectedResidual(baseline_config, edge_count, source_support)

    def log2feats(sequence):
        h = model.sasrec.log2feats(sequence)  # causal B x L x D
        source_vector = normalize(model.source_embedding(sequence), eps=1e-8)
        support = source_support.lookup(sequence, default=0)
        source_reliability = support / (support + 10.0)
        prefix_length = cumsum(sequence != 0, axis=1)
        gate_inputs = concat(h, log1p(support), log1p(prefix_length))
        gate = selected_gate_variant(gate_inputs)  # 1, global sigmoid, or linear sigmoid
        return Features(h, source_vector, sequence, gate, source_reliability)

    def predict_score(features, items):
        # Support B x L targets, B x L x K negatives, and final-state candidate chunks.
        # Explicitly broadcast features to candidate axes; never mix users or positions.
        base = dot(features.h, model.item_emb(items))
        target = normalize(model.target_embedding(items), eps=1e-8)
        transition = dot(features.source_vector, target)
        count = edge_count.lookup(features.source_ids, items, default=0)
        edge_reliability = count / (count + 3.0)
        scale = 2.0 * sigmoid(model.scale_parameter)
        residual = scale * features.gate * features.source_reliability
        residual = residual * edge_reliability * transition
        return base + residual

    for _, sequence, positive, negative in training_loader:
        features = log2feats(sequence)
        valid = (sequence != 0) & (positive != 0)
        pos_score = predict_score(features, positive)
        neg_score = predict_score(features, negative)
        loss = unchanged_baseline_loss(pos_score, neg_score, valid)
        optimize(loss)
        # Respect the prespecified epoch/compute cap and checkpoint schedule.

    save_under_trial_directory(model, counts, item_mapping, configuration)
    write_predictor_using_the_same_model_and_scoring_implementation()
    check_reload_candidate_and_full_catalog_score_parity()

# Run the four prespecified variants with matched compute/validation opportunities.
# Run DiagnosisProbe on the complete trained scorer; missing fields stay unavailable.
# Select solely by pinned four-category macro validation HR@10.
# No test labels, test metrics, external data, or pretrained weights enter search.

originality.positive: Candidate-specific distinct-user evidence and a bounded residual make the adaptation precise and distinguish its hypothesis from a generic transition branch.
originality.negative: FPMC, FOSSIL, SASRec's factorized Markov connection, and adaptive expert routing substantially precede the proposal; separate directed embeddings are not novel.

future_potential.positive: Provides a controlled framework for testing when population successor evidence complements individual sequence representations, with explicit fallback under sparse evidence.
future_potential.negative: Zero residual on unseen edges limits coverage, observed transitions can encode popularity or confounding, and compatibility and purchase completion remain unresolved.

code_difficulty.positive: The learned components remain small: two embedding tables, a linear gate and a bounded scale.
code_difficulty.negative: Candidate-specific sparse lookup, broadcasting, causal feature alignment, serialization, full-catalog chunking and diagnostic adaptation require substantial integration and parity checks.

related_work.title: Self-Attentive Sequential Recommendation
contributions: Provides the causal sequence encoder and candidate-scoring baseline.
Connects simplified attention-free, position-free configurations with untied embeddings to factorized Markov modeling.
limitations: Does not independently establish that an additive transition residual improves this benchmark.
Shared input/output embeddings do not imply symmetric overall sequence scores.

related_work.title: TGCL4SR
contributions: Combines temporal item-transition graph information with sequence modeling.
limitations: Does not establish gains for this pinned benchmark or certify product compatibility.

related_work.title: FamouSRec
contributions: Motivates adaptive routing among heterogeneous sequential recommendation experts.
limitations: Candidate-edge shrinkage and the bounded transition residual are proposed adaptations, not its reported architecture.

related_work.title: gSASRec
contributions: Addresses negative-sampling overconfidence through generalized binary cross-entropy and additional negatives.
limitations: Objective improvements do not directly establish current-intent alignment or gains under this evaluator.
Changing the objective simultaneously with the residual would confound attribution.

related_work.title: Factorizing Personalized Markov Chains for Next-Basket Recommendation
contributions: Combines preference and directed transition scores using distinct source and target factors.
Establishes direct precedent for additive preference–transition modeling.
limitations: Does not supply the proposed candidate-specific evidence gate.
Comparisons must account for objective differences, including its use of BPR.

related_work.title: FOSSIL: FactOrized Sequential Prediction with Item SImilarity ModeLs
contributions: Combines aggregated historical preferences with weighted recent-item transitions.
Uses factor sharing to support generalization under sparsity.
limitations: Does not establish that support-conditioned gating adds value to SASRec.
Its factorized generalization differs from restricting an empirical residual to observed edges.

related_work.title: NISER
contributions: Motivates examining representation norms and popularity bias in recommendation.
Supports considering normalized representations as a control on norm-driven scoring.
limitations: Does not validate this proposal's gate, shrinkage constants or bounded scale.
Normalization does not eliminate popularity shortcuts.

related_work.title: On Over-fitting in Model Selection and Subsequent Selection Bias in Performance Evaluation
contributions: Explains how repeated model selection can overfit validation noise.
Motivates prespecified ablations, selection opportunities and tie-breaking.
limitations: Prespecification cannot erase earlier adaptive search.
Fixed-seed bootstrap intervals do not correct winner-selection bias.

related_work.title: Show Your Work: Improved Reporting of Experimental Results
contributions: Motivates reporting performance alongside search and computational expenditure.
limitations: Does not prescribe an optimal allocation for this shared 43,200 GPU-second budget.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Shows why sampled-candidate metrics can disagree with full-catalog comparisons.
limitations: Does not authorize changing the pinned evaluator or replacing macro validation HR@10 as the selection metric.

related_work.title: SciPy bootstrap documentation
contributions: Documents bootstrap procedures applicable to paired per-user hit differences.
limitations: Requires available per-user outputs and correct pairing.
Does not account for training-seed uncertainty or adaptive model selection.
